# Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 23 (Bi-Vb Pc23)

**ID:** Bi-Vb Pc23

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Cīvarasibbana-sikkhāpada* ("Unstitching a robe") is the twenty-third rule in the *Pācittiya* chapter of the *Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga* in the Vinaya Piṭaka. According to the rule, a nun commits a *pācittiya* offence if, after having unstitched or caused another to unstitch the robe of a fellow nun, she does not sew it back together or arrange to have it sewn within a period of four to five days (*aññatra catūhapañcāhā*) [Hüsken 1997]. In the casuistry of the rule, even the mere intention not to sew the robe back together is treated as a *pācittiya*, while unstitching an article of requisition other than a robe incurs a *dukkaṭa* penalty [Hüsken 1997]. The non-offence clauses (*anāpatti*) exempt a nun if there is an intervening obstacle (*antarāya*), if she makes diligent efforts to complete the task but is unable to do so, or if the delay does not exceed the allotted four or five days [Hüsken 1997].

 Computational analysis via DharmaNexus indicates extensive Pali-internal text reuse with shared formulaic legal and casuistic phrases across the *Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga* (such as Pācittiya 45, 77, and 78, and Nissaggiya Pācittiya 3) and later Vinaya commentaries, as well as algorithmic alignments with Tibetan and Sanskrit monastic literature, notably the Sanskrit *Bhikṣuṇīvinaya* and the Tibetan *Bhikṣuṇīvinayavibhaṅga* (D0005) [DharmaNexus].
